Login

Sign-in needed two clicks

Fixed

Feedback: Staff had to press “Enter dashboard” twice to sign in.

  • Cause: after the first click the sign-in did succeed, but while the dashboard was loading the button changed back to “Enter dashboard” on the login page. On a slow connection it looked as if nothing had happened, so people clicked again.
  • The button now stays on “Signing in…” / “Opening dashboard…” until the dashboard appears, and cannot be pressed twice.
  • Email and password filled in by the browser’s autofill are now read correctly on the first click.
  • The dashboard is pre-loaded while the login page is open, so it opens faster.
TestWhat was checkedResult
TC-L.1one click on "Enter dashboard" signs in and opens the dashboardPassed
TC-L.2browser-autofilled email and password still sign in on the first clickPassed
TC-L.3a wrong password shows an error and the button can be used againPassed

Observed during the test run

  • Dashboard opened 2315 ms after a single click.
  • Button states seen after the click: Signing in....

3

Extra text printed on top of downloaded PDFs

Fixed

Feedback: Downloaded PDFs (the Credit Sheet and a dealer’s own PDF) showed extra text such as “All zones_Power Int.” at the top.

  • Cause: that text was the web browser’s own print header and footer (page title, date and web address), added whenever a page is saved through the browser’s Print → Save as PDF.
  • The Credit Sheet (Export PDF), a dealer’s ledger (new “Download PDF” button) and the dealer form (“PDF” button in Dealers) are now saved straight to a PDF file, without the print dialog, so the browser can no longer add anything to them.
  • The “Print” buttons still open the print dialog, now with the page margin set to zero, which removes the header in Chrome and Edge. Some phone browsers ignore this setting, so the download buttons are the recommended way to save a PDF.
TestWhat was checkedResult
TC-03.1the exported credit sheet PDF has no stray header textPassed
TC-03.2Print sheet asks the browser for no page margin, so it has no room for its title/URLPassed
TC-03.3a dealer's own ledger downloads as a PDF with no stray header textPassed
TC-03.4a dealer's form from the CRM downloads as a PDF with no stray header textPassed

Observed during the test run

  • First lines of the PDF: "POWER INTERNATIONAL BD", "CREDIT SHEET" — nothing above the company heading.
  • The stray text is the browser's own print header ("Credit Sheet", date, about:blank). Print sheet now sets a zero page margin, which Chrome and Edge on desktop honour by leaving the header out. Some phone browsers and Firefox ignore it, so files should be saved with Export PDF / Download PDF, which never go through the print dialog.
  • Downloaded ledger-E2E-PDF-Dealer-1790509031955.pdf directly (no print dialog): starts with the company heading, no title, date or URL.
  • Downloaded dealer-form-E2E-PDF-Dealer-1790509031955.pdf directly (no print dialog), with no title, date or URL on it.

Zone managers only see their own zone

Verified

Feedback: A person put in charge of a zone signs in with their own ID and only sees that zone’s dealers.

  • Tested with a real sign-in: a temporary Zone Manager account responsible for Dhaka Zone was created, used, and deleted again.
  • In Dealers (CRM) and the Credit Sheet that person only saw Dhaka Zone dealers; dealers of other zones were not listed, and the zone filter only offered their own zone.
  • They cannot open modules they were not given (Suppliers, Finance, User management). An admin still sees every zone.
  • A zone is assigned under Credit Sheet → Manage zones (“Responsible”), with the “Zone Manager” role under User & Role Management.
TestWhat was checkedResult
TC-07.1a zone manager sees only their own zone's dealers in the CRMPassed
TC-07.2the zone manager's credit sheet only has their zonePassed
TC-07.3the zone manager cannot open other modules they were not givenPassed
TC-07.4an admin still sees the dealers of every zonePassed

Observed during the test run

  • Signed in as a Zone Manager for Chattogram Zone: saw the Chattogram Zone dealer; none of the 7 Dhaka Zone dealers were listed.
  • Zone filter only offers: All zones, Chattogram Zone.
8

Mobile-friendly, clean interface

Verified

Feedback: Most staff use the ERP on a phone; it must work well on mobile and look clean and easy to understand.

  • Checked on a common Android phone size (Pixel 7): all main screens fit the screen with no sideways scrolling.
  • On phones the sidebar becomes a bottom tab bar (Home, Sales, Dealers, Credit, More) with large, easy-to-tap buttons; “More” opens every other module.
  • Readable text sizes, and input boxes large enough that phones do not zoom in when typing. Forms fit the screen and scroll.
TestWhat was checkedResult
TC-08.1every main screen fits the phone width without sideways scrollingPassed
TC-08.2phone navigation: bottom tab bar and a slide-out menu instead of the sidebarPassed
TC-08.3text is readable: body text at least 14px and inputs at least 16px (no zoom-in on focus)Passed
TC-08.4dialogs fit on the phone screen and can be scrolledPassed

Observed during the test run

  • Phone viewport: 412×839 (Pixel 7).
  • 7 screens checked, none wider than the 412px screen.
  • Bottom tab bar buttons are 64px high; the More menu opens every other module.
  • Body text 16px, inputs 16px, font: Inter.
  • Add dealer form is 388×807px on a 412×839 screen.

How the tests were run

  • Automated browser tests (Playwright, Chromium) on 27 September 2026, against a production build of the ERP connected to the live database.
  • Desktop checks at 1280×720; phone checks on a Pixel 7 screen (412×839).
  • Records created for testing (dealers, a supplier, a temporary Zone Manager account) were given “E2E” names, visible in some screenshots, and removed again after the run. A final check confirmed nothing was left behind.
  • Downloaded PDFs were checked for page size (A4), content, and that nothing is printed above the company heading.
